In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new inhibitors of the enzyme tryptophan 5-hydroxylase (tryptophan hydroxylation) which is the key enzyme in the biosynthesis of serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5HT).

the structural studies of condensation compounds of dopamine and indolamines as inhibitors of TPH, and the effects of the catechol iso-quinolines on the activity of TPH were evaluated in order to determine the structures of compounds associated with the modulation of this enzyme.
the development of a novel class of inhibitors of TPH and their potential application in the treatment of psychiatric disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the catecholic structure of the condensation products between dopamine and indole derivatives is a prerequisite for the inhibition of TPH activity.
the dopamine-derived catechols are potent and selective inhibitors of TPH, and that they are likely to be endogenous substances that modulate the synthesis of serotonin.
the dopamine-derived catechols are potent non-competitive inhibitors of TPH, which may play a significant role in the regulation of the biosynthesis of 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin).

the catechols, such as 6,7-dimethoxy-1-methyl-1, 2,3, 4-tetra-hydroisoquinoline and 6,7- dihydroxy-1-methylisoquinoline, inhibit TPH activity in a non-competitive manner.
